quote: Our most recent bill, I think, was, like, $2.02 42 or something like that. I just opened it this morning, which is kinda what prompted the whole conversation.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep both a bill figure and the origin story (opened the bill that morning, prompted the call) in one breath — an unusually rich anchor. Rep responds with 'Oh, gotcha. Okay. Gotcha.' and moves to the next verify question without reflecting the number back or tying it to the appointment's purpose.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read is more supported than a strategic-deferral read here: the rep's immediate pivot to 'is this your first time looking at solar' shows no signal of intent to circle back to the bill figure later in the call, and it never resurfaces.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to acknowledge the specific number and the trigger event together — e.g. reflecting that opening a bill like that is exactly the kind of moment worth acting on — before moving to the next verify item. This costs seconds and makes the appointment purpose sticky.

quote: does 1,200 kilowatts a month sound, like, normal?
stewart_read: Customer is asking an open, curious question about his own usage — a strong invitation to build anticipation for the design review. Rep answers factually ('a little bit more on the higher side') and redirects to needing the actual bill, which is accurate but flat.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic deferral is plausible since the rep does correctly redirect to needing the bill for accuracy, consistent with setter scope discipline around not giving pricing/technical detail. But the redirect misses the chance to build curiosity about what the design will show him.
coaching_implication: When a customer asks a self-comparison question like this, a stronger move ties it forward: something like 'that's exactly what the specialist's design will nail down for you' plus a forward-pulling hook, rather than just naming the range and citing the bill requirement.

quote: I would definitely want to be want to be there, you know, obviously, and not just my wife. You know what I mean? So
stewart_read: Dominic is signaling that he wants to be present alongside his wife (who is also on the title) rather than leave it to her. This is a co-owner-inclusion moment the rep should lock explicitly.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is stronger: the rep replies 'Sure. 100%.' and 'For sure. 100%.' then moves straight into stating this will be a phone call, never confirming that both Dominic and his wife will be on the appointment together.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly confirm both spouses will be on the call at the booked time, per protocols.spouse_decision — a quick 'so we'll have both you and your wife on the line at 4' closes the loop that was left open here.

quote: And we're just kind of ex exploring options right now. Like, we're not committed to, like, you know, we're definitely going to solar and you know?
stewart_read: Customer explicitly caveats the booking to manage expectations, wanting to avoid being read as a hot lead who's ready to sign. Rep validates this well without arguing.
coaching_implication: This caveat should travel directly into the handoff brief so the closer doesn't open with an assumptive close that resets the customer's guard.

quote: once I get that bill from you, I'll just shoot you a confirmation text with the date and time of the meeting.
stewart_read: The rep's own language makes the appointment's written confirmation contingent on a bill the customer says he won't be able to send until 'sometime later this evening.' This is the clearest evidence the booking is not yet fully locked at call's end.
coaching_implication: Flag this as the reason the outcome should be read as tentative rather than booked — the manager should check whether the bill and confirmation text actually went out before crediting this as a solid sit.

quote: I guess one question is, is this like a a lease thing, or do we own the panels, or how how does how does that wall work?
stewart_read: Customer asks a financing/ownership-structure question late in the call. Rep correctly declines to answer in depth and redirects to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: This is a positive example, not a miss — the rep says 'there's different options you can look at, and they'll be able to go over everything,' which is the correct escape hatch rather than scope creep.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model response when coaching other reps on setter_scope_discipline — the rep held the line here without over-explaining lease vs. ownership mechanics.

quote: Honestly, I I run a business, so there's really no telling.
stewart_read: Customer flags unpredictable scheduling due to seasonal business demands ('spring rush,' fourteen-hour days), which is relevant context for why a locked time may still shift.
coaching_implication: This is useful handoff context about schedule volatility, not a claim about in-call distraction — the closer should be aware the customer's availability may be fluid given his work season, and a reminder text closer to the appointment may help hold the slot.
